correctness.rationale: For every k>=1 and S>=1, B(N+a)/(B(N)B(a)) is a ratio of 3-adic units 1+3^k Z_3 when v3(N)>=k+floor(log_3(2a)); this yields separated-block multiplicativity modulo 3^k. For N=3^R, the b_R=2 prod_{i=1}^{N-1}(1+N/i) expansion has exactly the two exceptional modulo-9 factors at i=N/3,2N/3, whose product is 10=1(mod9), so b_R=2(mod9) and by LTE has exact order 2*3^(k-1) modulo 3^k. Infinite pigeonhole yields a repeating unit u among b_R residues along unbounded exponents; spaced choices yield B(A_t+sum 3^Ri)=B(A_t)u^j mod3^k. The seed A_t=3^S(3^t+1)/2 for t>=1 (or 3^S for t=0) has exactly t ternary carries, so v3(B(A_t))=t; multiplication by u^j traverses all valuation-t units (0<=t<k), while t=k supplies zero. For each fixed residue, infinitely many j in a suitable congruence class and arbitrarily large spaced exponents supply distinct indices. If S>=k, C_{N-1}=B(N)/(2(2N-1))=-B(N)/2 mod3^k for constructed N, transferring all classes. Independent exact checks: seeds t<=8, primitive roots R<=8 and k<=6, 825 separated-block instances, all classes modulo 3,9,27,81,243 among first 30000 Catalans. Finite checks corroborate only; analytical argument proves all k.
residual_risks: No density or effective bound; the infinitude construction is existential via an infinite repeated-residue subsequence.
The source checker independently confirms examples only and is not a proof of unbounded k.

evidence: Krattenthaler--Muller Theorem 37 is a finite-modulus generating-function expansion and Theorems 38--39 give explicit modulo-27/9 formulas; they do not state all-residue reachability for every exponent.

Barat--Grabner Theorem 7 equidistributes p-free binomial coefficients among all pairs (n,j) with 0<=j<=n<N. This 2D population does not constrain the central diagonal j=n/2, much less Catalan normalization.
Sun--Zhang 2008/2011 abstract covers binomial(n,k) with specified fixed lower k as n varies; k=n on a central diagonal is not fixed.
Rowland--Yassawi Theorem 1.2 gives a finite automaton for each prescribed modulus, not universal surjectivity as its explicit Open Question 3.6 confirms.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Stronger general algorithms for computing modular coefficients and full-Pascal-array equidistribution do not mathematically imply that each residue occurs among central coefficients at arbitrarily 3-divisible indices. A general block-multiplicative theorem specialized to the diagonal could still implicitly cover the result and is a residual risk.

The explicitly open question in 2015 is strong evidence of the gap at that date, not proof nobody solved it later.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original: proves the all-exponent Catalan 3-adic density and infinitely many witnesses, answering the explicitly stated Rowland--Yassawi Open Question 3.6. Krattenthaler--Muller give 3-power coefficient formulas, Burns gives prime-modulus surjectivity, and Rampersad--Shallit analyze prime-modulus Catalan automata; none of their inspected statements proves the uniform 3^k surjectivity. Barat--Grabner equidistribution concerns the full triangular Pascal array (n,j), not the constrained central diagonal (2N,N); Sun--Zhang concerns fixed lower binomial index. Unindexed implicit coverage remains a historical-priority risk, not a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Historical priority is best-of-knowledge: an unindexed proof from after the 2015 open question could exist.
General block-digit or 3-adic binomial congruence machinery might yield the same result after a non-obvious diagonal specialization.
Sun--Zhang full paper and older specialized catalogues not exhaustively read; its fixed-index scope is different.
No positive natural density or effective least-index bound is proved; do not infer either from infinitude.

value.rationale: This is the exact published forbidden-residue question for Catalan numbers modulo every power of 3, not a single finite census or routine fixed-modulus calculation. It proves a strong complete natural classification: every 3-adic residue neighbourhood is hit infinitely often, with a reusable separated-block and primitive-root mechanism. The precise mathematical gap was explicitly recorded as Open Question 3.6 by Rowland--Yassawi; first-index bounds or density are not claimed.
residual_risks: The technique does not furnish natural densities or computationally efficient witness bounds; these limitations do not diminish the complete reachability theorem.
